additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional disorder is characterized by one or more persistent delusions lasting at least a month (often many months or years) in the absence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized thought, or marked negative symptoms, and with relatively preserved overall functioning outside the delusional themes. The delusions are fixed false beliefs that remain resistant to clear contradictory evidence and are not better explained by mood episodes, substance use, or another psychotic disorder. Content can involve persecution, jealousy, somatic concerns, grandiosity, or erotomanic ideas, and behavior may be subtly shaped by these beliefs while still appearing outwardly organized. Onset is often insidious in mid to later adulthood, and patients frequently present only after family, employers, or legal systems become involved because the person does not recognize the beliefs as pathological.

patient.stressor: Peggy’s difficulties emerged gradually after a tense period in her marriage when she and her husband were juggling college costs for their eldest child and caring for her aging mother. A minor billing discrepancy at work, which was quickly corrected, seemed to trigger a growing preoccupation that certain members of her church circle and even her sister‑in‑law were quietly orchestrating situations to undermine her reputation as "honest with money." Over nine months, she increasingly interpreted missed invitations, casual comments at potlucks, and small errors in the office as part of a coordinated effort against her, though she continued to perform her job and household roles with outward competence. When she confronted a longtime friend at the library about being part of this supposed scheme and the friend tearfully suggested she talk to a doctor, Peggy—torn between her conviction and her desire to keep the peace—agreed to see a psychiatrist at her pastor’s recommendation.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel like certain people in my family and church are quietly working together against me, and no one believes me when I say it.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Ever since that mix‑up with the bill at work, I’m convinced my sister‑in‑law and a couple of ladies from church have been quietly spreading doubts about whether I can be trusted with money, and no matter how many people tell me it’s just in my head, all the little things they do—like leaving me off group texts or making side comments when I walk up—fit too perfectly for it to be a coincidence.

add_requirements.Functioning is not markedly impaired apa: I still get to work on time, keep up with the billing, and take care of my mom and the house like I always have, but anything that involves those particular people—I’ll avoid their events, argue with my husband about them, or spend hours replaying their comments in my head.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve started skipping some family get‑togethers and church gatherings if I think those women will be there, and it’s caused tension with my husband and kids who say I’m overreacting and acting distant from everyone.
add_requirements.duration: This has been building ever since that small billing mistake at work, so it’s been going on for about nine months now.
